binaries.name: journalctl
binaries.why: Read a systemd journal from a file or directory. The journal is a binary format and nothing else reads it reliably.

install.brew: not available on macOS; analyse on a Linux host

binaries.name: debsums
binaries.why: Compare every packaged file on a Debian host against the distribution's own hashes: the fastest way to find a replaced binary.

binaries.name: rpm
binaries.why: rpm -Va does the same job on a Red Hat family host, and reports which attribute changed.

binaries.name: ausearch
binaries.why: Read the kernel audit log, where the estate had auditd on: execve with arguments, and file access by rule.

binaries.name: debugfs
binaries.why: Read ext2/3/4 internals the Sleuth Kit does not surface: the inode's creation time, extent trees, and the journal.

binaries.name: xfs_db
binaries.why: Inspect XFS superblocks, allocation groups, inodes and free-space metadata in read-only mode; The Sleuth Kit does not provide complete XFS coverage.

install.brew: not available on macOS; analyse on a Linux host

binaries.name: btrfs
binaries.why: Read Btrfs superblocks, trees, subvolumes and device membership without mounting the evidence.

install.brew: not available on macOS; analyse on a Linux host

binaries.name: lvs
binaries.why: Enumerate Linux LVM physical volumes, volume groups and logical volumes when a disk's partition table only exposes an LVM container.
